mountApp builds a real <main id="pk-main"> landmark at runtime (js/app/shell.js) inside the pk-app-shell it mounts into #app; A7 scans only the static HTML text and cannot see DOM built by JS. Adding a static <main> wrapper around #app would instead create a nested/duplicate <main> landmark once mountApp mounts (a real accessibility regression), so that is not a safe fix here.
Same as index.html: mountApp builds the real <main> landmark at runtime; a static <main> wrapper would nest landmarks once mounted. See #518.

This is the framework's own required base stylesheet (../../plainkit.css: tokens, reset, the u-sr-only utility the shell itself uses), not app-authored CSS; a plain static HTML entry with no bundler has no other way to load it. The design doc's own rule table (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-conformance-audit-cli-design.md, S1 row) lists an `allowCss: ['app.css']` config knob meant for exactly this kind of case, but it was never implemented in core/tools/audit/families/s-rules.mjs (checked: no allowCss reference anywhere in core/tools/audit). Using the generic allow-list here instead of inventing a local workaround.
